## What this workflow demonstrates

This is a demo example of the fetch → enrich → re-ingest pattern in Enterspeed: taking a piece of already-transformed content, adding extra data to it via an external process, and feeding that extra data back in as a separate, linked entity — without touching the original source entity.

[Enterspeed Docs](https://docs.enterspeed.com/api-reference/delivery/get-content-by-url-ids-or-handles)

### The Enterspeed concepts at play

* Source Entity — the raw data as it exists in the originating system (here, a `product`). You never write enrichment data directly onto it.
* Schema — a deployed transformation that turns a Source Entity into a View. The `product` schema declares what a product's output should look like.
* Reference by originId — schemas can pull in data from other entities by ID, without those entities needing to exist yet at deploy time. That's the mechanism this workflow relies on: the product schema always requests `productMetadata → byOriginId('{originId}-metadata')`, whether or not that enriched entity has been created.

### Why a second, separate entity instead of updating the product directly

Because the product schema references a distinct `originId ({originId}-metadata)`, enrichment can be produced independently — by any process, on any schedule — and simply ingested under that naming convention. The moment it exists, Enterspeed resolves the reference and the enriched data shows up in the product's View automatically. Nothing needs to re-touch or redeploy the product's own schema or source data as long the reference to the schema already exists.

## The flow, step by step

1. Fetch the product's current View via the Delivery API (Get content). The URL `/products/trailblazer-hiking-sneaker` and the H. C. Andersen copy further down are specific to the n8n demo tenant — swap them for a URL and content that exist in your own Enterspeed environment (see CONTRIBUTING.md).
2. Check whether it's already contians metadata — skip if so, to avoid redundant work.
3. Transform: generate the enrichment payload (in this demo, a static value — swap this step for a real enrichment call, e.g. [Speedtrain](https://www.enterspeed.com/products/services/speedtrain-content-accelerator) or an LLM).
4. Save it as a new entity, `product-metadata`, via the Ingest API.
5. Wait: ingest is asynchronous, so pause briefly before reading back (you'd use a Enterspeed Webhook on deploy instead of a fixed wait).
6. Re-fetch the product's View — it should now include `seoMetaDescription` and `enriched_data`, resolved via the reference.
7. Validate the result.
